video.title: TimelineEntry, WidgetFamily & Timeline | Day 184
video.description:
Learn to explain how WidgetKit decides what a home screen widget shows and when: TimelineEntry, WidgetFamily & Timeline, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
TimelineEntry - A protocol for the data of a widget at one moment in time, with a date.
WidgetFamily - An enum for the sizes of a widget, such as small, medium and large.
Timeline - A list of widget entries with dates, and a rule for when to ask for more.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain TimelineEntry, WidgetFamily and Timeline in English?

dialogue.title: A habit widget

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I am starting a home screen widget for my habit app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A widget shows data from a TimelineEntry. It has a `date` and your own values.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why does the TimelineEntry need a `date`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: WidgetKit uses the date to know when to show each entry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I give it a list of entries?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, put them in a Timeline. It has the entries and a rule, like `.never` in the code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I made one entry, and the widget never changed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add more entries to the Timeline, with later dates.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And for sizes? Is there a WidgetFamily?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, like `.systemSmall`. Check the WidgetFamily in your view and change the layout.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can one view work in all sizes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, but check the WidgetFamily first, so small widgets stay simple.
